What changed: iaso now treats some results of a test that runs with several inputs as out of date. If the newest run of that test leaves one of its inputs out, iaso throws away that input's older result. The goal was to handle inputs that were renamed or deleted. But the new code assumes every run tries all of a test's inputs, and it doesn't check that this is true. A run often tries only some of them, for example when only certain cases are picked or a single case is rerun. When that happens, a still-failing case disappears even though nothing passed it, and the merge can go green while a failure is still there.
